I am willing to think that in this word of Christ there is an intimation of mercy Christ had yet in store for this young gentleman, who was now gone away sorrowful; it was not impossible to God yet to recover him, and bring him to a better mind. <div eID="gen23020" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23021" type="x-p"/> II. Peter took occasion from hence to enquire what <hi type="italic">they</hi> should get by it, who had come up to these terms, upon which this young man broke with Christ, and had left all to follow him, <reference osisRef="Matt.19.27">v. 27</reference>, &c. We have here the disciples' expectations from Christ, and his promises to them. <div eID="gen23021" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23022" type="x-p"/> 1. We have their expectations from Christ; Peter, in the name of the rest, signifies that they depended upon him for something considerable in lieu of what they had left for him; <hi type="italic">Behold, we have forsaken all, and have followed thee; what shall we have therefore?</hi> Christ had promised the young man, that, if he would sell all, and come and follow him, he should <hi type="italic">have treasure in heaven;</hi> now Peter desires to know, <div eID="gen23022" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23023" type="x-p"/> (1.) Whether they had sufficiently come up to those terms: they had not sold all (for they had many of them wives and families to provide for), but they had <hi type="italic">forsaken all;</hi> they had not given it to the poor, but they had renounced it as far as it might be any way a hindrance to them in serving Christ. Note, When we hear what are the characters of those that shall be saved, it concerns us to enquire whether we, through grace, answer those characters. Now Peter hopes that, as to the main scope and intendment of the condition, they had come up to it, for God had wrought in them a holy contempt of the world and the things that are seen, in comparison with Christ and the things that are not seen; and how this must be evidenced, no certain rule can be given, but according as we are called. <div eID="gen23023" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23024" type="x-p"/> Lord, saith Peter, <hi type="italic">we have forsaken all.</hi> Alas! it was but a poor <hi type="italic">all</hi> that they had forsaken; one of them had indeed quitted a place in the custom-house, but Peter and the most of them had only left a few boats and nets, and the appurtenances of a poor fishing-trade; and yet observe how Peter there speaks of it, as it had been some mighty thing; <hi type="italic">Behold, we have forsaken all.</hi> Note, We are too apt to make the most of our services and sufferings, our expenses and losses, for Christ, and to think we have made him much our debtor. However, Christ does not upbraid them with this; though it was but little that they had forsaken, yet it was their <hi type="italic">all,</hi> like the widow's two mites, and was as dear to them as if it had been more, and therefore Christ took it kindly that they left it to follow him; for he accepts <hi type="italic">according to what a man hath.</hi> <div eID="gen23024" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23025" type="x-p"/> (2.) Whether therefore they might expect <hi type="italic">that treasure</hi> which the young man shall have if he will sell all. "Lord," saith Peter, "shall <hi type="italic">we</hi> have it, who have left all?" All people are for what they can get; and Christ's followers are allowed to consult their own true interest, and to ask, <hi type="italic">What shall we have?</hi> Christ <hi type="italic">looked at the joy set before him,</hi> and Moses <hi type="italic">at the recompence of reward.</hi> For this end it is set before us, that <hi type="italic">by a patient continuance in well-doing</hi> we may seek for it. Christ encourages us to ask what we shall gain by leaving all to follow him; that we may see he doth not call us to our prejudice, but unspeakably to our advantage. As it is the language of an obediential faith to ask, "What shall we <hi type="italic">do?</hi>" with an eye to the precepts; so it is of a hoping, trusting faith, to ask, "What shall we <hi type="italic">have?</hi>" with an eye to the promises. But observe, The disciples had long since left all to engage themselves in the service of Christ, and yet never till now asked, <hi type="italic">What shall we have?</hi> Though there was no visible prospect of advantage by it, they were so well assured of his goodness, that they knew they should not lose by him at last, and therefore referred themselves to him, in what way he would make up their losses to them; minded their work, and asked not what should be their wages. Note, It honours Christ, to trust him and serve him, and not to bargain with him. Now that this young man was gone from Christ to his possessions, it was time for them to think which they should take to, what they should trust to. When we see what others keep by their hypocrisy and apostasy, it is proper for us to consider what we hope, through grace, to gain, not <hi type="italic">for,</hi> but <hi type="italic">by,</hi> our sincerity and constancy, and then we shall see more reason to pity them than to envy them. <div eID="gen23025" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23026" type="x-p"/> 2. We have here Christ's promises to them, and to all others that tread in the steps of their faith and obedience. What there was either of vain-glory or of vain hopes in that which Peter said, Christ overlooks, and is not extreme to mark it, but takes this occasion to give the bond of a <hi type="italic">promise,</hi> <div eID="gen23026" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23027" type="x-p"/> (1.) To his immediate followers, <reference osisRef="Matt.19.28">v. 28</reference>. They had signalized their respect to him, as the first that followed him, and to them he promises not only <hi type="italic">treasure,</hi> but <hi type="italic">honour,</hi> in heaven; and here they have a grant or patent for it from him who is the fountain of honour in that kingdom; <hi type="italic">Ye which have followed me in the regeneration shall sit upon twelve thrones.</hi> Observe, <div eID="gen23027" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23028" type="x-p"/> [1.] The <hi type="italic">preamble</hi> to the patent, or the <hi type="italic">consideration</hi> of the grant, which, as usual, is a recital of their services; "You have followed me in the regeneration, and therefore this will I do for you." The time of Christ's appearing in this world was a time of regeneration, of reformation (<reference osisRef="Heb.9.10">Heb. ix. 10</reference>), when old things began to pass away, and all things to look new. The disciples had followed Christ when the church was yet in the embryo state, when the gospel temple was but in the framing, when they had more of the work and service of the apostles than of the dignity and power that belonged to their office. Now they followed Christ with constant fatigue, when few did; and therefore on them he will put particular marks of honour. Note, Christ hath special favour for those who begin early with him, who trust him further than they can see him, as they did who <hi type="italic">followed him in the regeneration.</hi> Observe, Peter spoke of their forsaking <hi type="italic">all,</hi> to follow him, Christ only speaks of their <hi type="italic">following him,</hi> which was the main matter. <div eID="gen23028" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23029" type="x-p"/> [2.] The <hi type="italic">date</hi> of their honour, which fixes the time when it should commence; not immediately from the day of the date of <hi type="italic">these presents,</hi> no, they must continue a while in obscurity, as they were. But <hi type="italic">when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory;</hi> and to this some refer that, <hi type="italic">in the regeneration;</hi> "You who now have followed me, shall, in the regeneration, be thus dignified." Christ's second coming will be a regeneration, when there shall be <hi type="italic">new heavens, and a new earth, and the restitution of all things.</hi> All that partake of the regeneration in grace (<reference osisRef="John.3.3">John iii. 3</reference>) shall partake of the regeneration in glory; for as grace is the first resurrection (<reference osisRef="Rev.20.6">Rev. xx. 6</reference>), so glory is the second regeneration. <div eID="gen23029" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23030" type="x-p"/> Now their honour being adjourned till the Son of man's sitting in the throne of his glory, intimates, <hi type="italic">First,</hi> That they must stay for their advancement till then. Note, As long as our Master's glory is delayed, it is fit that ours should be so too, and that we should wait for it with an earnest expectation, as of a <hi type="italic">hope not seen.</hi> <reference osisRef="Rom.8.19">Rom. viii. 19</reference>. We must live, and work, and suffer, in faith, and hope, and patience, which therefore must be tried by these delays. <hi type="italic">Secondly,</hi> That they must share with Christ in his advancement; their honour must be a communion with him in his honour. They, having suffered with a suffering Jesus, must reign with a reigning Jesus, for both here and hereafter Christ will be <hi type="italic">all in all;</hi> we must <hi type="italic">be where he is</hi> (<reference osisRef="John.12.26">John xii. 26</reference>), must <hi type="italic">appear with him</hi> (<reference osisRef="Col.3.4">Col. iii. 4</reference>); and this will be an abundant recompence not only for our loss, but for the delay; and when our Lord comes, we shall receive not only <hi type="italic">our own,</hi> but our own <hi type="italic">with usury.</hi> The longest voyages make the richest returns. <div eID="gen23030" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23031" type="x-p"/> [3.] The honour itself hereby granted; <hi type="italic">Ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.</hi> It is hard to determine the particular sense of this promise, and whether it was not to have many accomplishments, which I see no harm in admitting. <hi type="italic">First,</hi> When Christ is ascended to the right hand of the Father, and sits on the throne of his glory, then the apostles shall receive power by the Holy Ghost (<reference osisRef="Acts.1.8">Acts i. 8</reference>); shall be so much advanced above themselves as they are now, that they shall think themselves upon thrones, in promoting the gospel; they shall deliver it with authority, as a judge from the bench; they shall then have their commission enlarged, and shall publish the laws of Christ, by which the church, God's spiritual Israel (<reference osisRef="Gal.6.16">Gal. vi. 16</reference>), shall be governed, and <hi type="italic">Israel according to the flesh,</hi> that continues in infidelity, with all others that do likewise, shall be condemned. The honour and power given them, may be explained by <reference osisRef="Jer.1.19">Jer. i. 19</reference>, <hi type="italic">See, I have set thee over the nations;</hi> and <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.4">Ezek; xx. 4</reference>, <hi type="italic">Wilt thou judge them?</hi> and <reference osisRef="Dan.7.18">Dan. vii. 18</reference>, <hi type="italic">The saints shall take the kingdom;</hi> and <reference osisRef="Rev.12.1">Rev. xii. 1</reference>, where the doctrine of Christ is called <hi type="italic">a crown of twelve stars. Secondly,</hi> When Christ appears for the destruction of Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.31">ch. xxiv. 31</reference>), then shall he send the apostles to judge the Jewish nation, because in that destruction their predictions, according to the word of Christ, would be accomplished. <hi type="italic">Thirdly,</hi> Some think it has reference to the conversion of the Jews, which is yet to come, at the latter end of the world, after the fall of antichrist; so Dr. Whitby; and that "it respects the apostles' government of <hi type="italic">the twelve tribes of Israel,</hi> not by a resurrection of their persons, but by a reviviscence of that Spirit which resided in them, and of that purity and knowledge which they delivered to the world, and, chiefly, by admission of their gospel to be the standard of their faith and the direction of their lives." <hi type="italic">Fourthly,</hi> It is certainly to have its full accomplishment at the second coming of Jesus Christ, when <hi type="italic">the saints</hi> in general <hi type="italic">shall judge the world,</hi> and the twelve apostles especially, as assessors with Christ, <hi type="italic">in the judgment of the great day,</hi> when all the world shall receive their final doom, and they shall ratify and applaud the sentence. But the <hi type="italic">tribe</hi> of Israel are named, partly because the number of the apostles was designedly the same with the number of the tribes; partly because the apostles were Jews, befriended them most, but were most spitefully persecuted by them; and it intimates that the saints will judge their acquaintance and kindred according to the flesh, and will, in the great day, judge those they had a kindness for; will judge their persecutors, who in this world judged them. <div eID="gen23031" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23032" type="x-p"/> But the general intendment of this promise is, to show the glory and dignity reserved for the saints in heaven, which will be an abundant recompence for the disgrace they suffered here in Christ's cause. There are higher degrees of glory for those that have done and suffered most. The apostles in this world were hurried and tossed, there they shall sit down at rest and ease; here <hi type="italic">bonds, and afflictions, and deaths, did abide them,</hi> but there they <hi type="italic">shall sit on thrones of glory;</hi> here they were dragged to the bar, there they shall be advanced to the bench; here the twelve tribes of Israel trampled upon them, there they shall tremble before them. And will not this be recompence enough to make up all their losses and expenses for Christ? <reference osisRef="Luke.22.29">Luke xxii. 29</reference>. <div eID="gen23032" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23033" type="x-p"/> [4.] The ratification of this grant; it is firm, it is inviolably immutably sure; for Christ hath said, "<hi type="italic">Verily I say unto you, I the Amen, the faithful Witness,</hi> who am empowered to make this grant, I have said it, and it cannot be disannulled." <div eID="gen23033" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23034" type="x-p"/> (2.) Here is a promise to all others that should in like manner leave all to follow Christ. It was not peculiar to the apostles, to be thus preferred, but <hi type="italic">this honour have all his saints.</hi> Christ will take care they shall none of them lose by him (<reference osisRef="Matt.19.29">v. 29</reference>); <hi type="italic">Every one that has forsaken</hi> any thing for Christ, <hi type="italic">shall receive.</hi> <div eID="gen23034" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23035" type="x-p"/> [1.] Losses for Christ are here supposed. Christ had told them that his disciples must deny themselves in all that is done to them in this world; now here he specifies particulars; for it is good to count upon the worst. If they have not forsaken all, as the apostles did, yet they have forsaken a great deal, houses suppose, and have turned themselves out, to wander in deserts; or dear relations, that would not go with them, to follow Christ; these are particularly mentioned, as hardest for a tender gracious spirit to part with; <hi type="italic">brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children;</hi> and <hi type="italic">lands</hi> are added in the close; the profits of which were the support of the family. <div eID="gen23035" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23036" type="x-p"/> Now, <hi type="italic">First,</hi> the loss of these things is supposed to be <hi type="italic">for Christ's name's sake;</hi> else he doth not oblige himself to make it up. Many forsake brethren, and wife, and children, in humour and passion, as <hi type="italic">the bird that wanders from her nest;</hi> that is a sinful desertion. But if we forsake them <hi type="italic">for Christ's sake,</hi> because we cannot keep them and keep a good conscience, we must either quit them, or quit our interest in Christ; if we do not quit our concern for them, or our duty to them, but our comfort in them, and will do it rather than deny Christ, and this with an eye to him, and to his will and glory, this is that which shall be thus recompensed. It is not the suffering, but the cause, that makes both the martyr and the confessor. <div eID="gen23036" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23037" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">Secondly,</hi> It is supposed to be a great loss; and yet Christ undertakes to make up, for he is able to do it, be it ever so great. See the barbarity of the persecutors, that they stripped innocent people of all they had, for no other crime than their adherence to Christ! See the patience of the persecuted; and the strength of their love to Christ, which was such as all these waters could not quench! <div eID="gen23037" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23038" type="x-p"/> [2.] A recompence of these losses is here secured. Thousands have dealt with Christ, and have trusted him far; but never any one lost by him, never any one but was an unspeakable gainer by him, when the account came to be balanced. Christ here gives his word for it, that he will not only indemnify his suffering servants, and save them harmless, but will abundantly reward them. Let them make a schedule of their losses for Christ, and they shall be sure to receive, <div eID="gen23038" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23039" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">First, A hundred-fold in this life;</hi> sometimes in <hi type="italic">kind,</hi> in the things themselves which they have parted with. God will raise up for his suffering servants more friends, that will be so to them for Christ's sake, than they have left that were so for their own sakes. The apostles, wherever they came, met with those that were kind to them, and entertained them, and opened their hearts and doors to them. However, they <hi type="italic">shall receive a hundred-fold,</hi> in <hi type="italic">kindness,</hi> in those things that are abundantly better and more valuable. Their graces shall increase, their comforts abound, they shall have tokens of God's love, more free communion with him, more full communications from him, clearer foresights, and sweeter foretastes, of <hi type="italic">the glory to be revealed;</hi> and then they may truly say, they have received a hundred times more comfort in God and Christ than they could have had in <hi type="italic">wife, or children.</hi> <div eID="gen23039" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23040" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">Secondly,</hi> Eternal life at last. The former is reward enough, if there were no more; cent. per cent. is great profit; what then is a hundred to one? But this comes in over and above, as it were, into the bargain. The <hi type="italic">life</hi> here promised includes in it all the comforts of life in the highest degree, and all <hi type="italic">eternal.</hi> Now if we could but mix faith with the promise, and trust Christ for the performance of it, surely we should think nothing too much to do, nothing too hard to suffer, nothing too dear to part with, for him. <div eID="gen23040" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23041" type="x-p"/> Our Saviour, in the last verse, obviates a mistake of some, as if pre-eminence in glory went by precedence in time, rather than the measure and degree of grace. No; <hi type="italic">Many that are first, shall be last, and the last, first,</hi> <reference osisRef="Matt.19.30">v. 30</reference>. God will cross his hands; will <hi type="italic">reveal that to babes,</hi> which he <hi type="italic">hid from the wise and prudent;</hi> will reject unbelieving Jews and receive believing Gentiles. The heavenly inheritance is not given as earthly inheritances commonly are, by seniority of age, and priority of birth, but according to God's pleasure. This is the text of another sermon, which we shall meet with in the next chapter.  <chapter eID="Matt.19"/> <div eID="gen23041" type="x-p"/>

entries.e623c7560a3dcba12a6b6502f2c8ca19362bcaf0: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13694"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 19</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Matt.19.1-Matt.19.12">Mt 19:1-12</reference>. Final Departure from Galilee--Divorce. ( = <reference osisRef="Mark.10.1-Mark.10.12">Mr 10:1-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.9.51">Lu 9:51</reference>).</title> <div sID="gen26255" type="x-p"/> Farewell to Galilee (<reference osisRef="Matt.19.1">Mt 19:1</reference>, 2).<div eID="gen26255" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26256" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13694"/><hi type="bold">1. And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee--</hi>This marks a very solemn period in our Lord's public ministry. So slightly is it touched here, and in the corresponding passage of Mark (<reference osisRef="Mark.10.1">Mr 10:1</reference>), that few readers probably note it as the Redeemer's Farewell to Galilee, which however it was. See on the sublime statement of Luke (<reference osisRef="Luke.9.51">Lu 9:51</reference>), which relates to the same transition stage in the progress of our Lord's work.<div eID="gen26256" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26257" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and came into the coasts--</hi>or, boundaries<div eID="gen26257" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26258" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of Judea beyond Jordan--</hi>that is, to the further, or east side of the Jordan, into Perea, the dominions of Herod Antipas. But though one might conclude from our Evangelist that our Lord went straight from the one region to the other, we know from the other Gospels that a considerable time elapsed between the departure from the one and the arrival at the other, during which many of the most important events in our Lord's public life occurred--probably a large part of what is recorded in <reference osisRef="Luke.9.51">Lu 9:51</reference>, onward to <reference osisRef="Luke.18.15">Lu 18:15</reference>, and part of Joh 7:2-11:54. <div eID="gen26258" type="x-p"/>
entries.f6d9d0b5f98ec031230910de2629b0d0fef80a74: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13695"/><div sID="gen26259" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13695"/><hi type="bold">2. And great multitudes followed him; and he healed them there--</hi>Mark says further (<reference osisRef="Mark.10.1">Mr 10:1</reference>), that "as He was wont, He taught them there." What we now have on the subject of divorce is some of that teaching.<div eID="gen26259" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26260" type="x-p"/> Divorce (<reference osisRef="Matt.19.3-Matt.19.12">Mt 19:3-12</reference>). <div eID="gen26260" type="x-p"/>
entries.ae41a9a00602f8fb46742017ccfc0bba7013782b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13696"/><div sID="gen26261" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13696"/><hi type="bold">3. Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?--</hi>Two rival schools (as we saw on <reference osisRef="Matt.5.31">Mt 5:31</reference>) were divided on this question--a delicate one, as De Wette pertinently remarks, in the dominions of Herod Antipas. <div eID="gen26261" type="x-p"/>
entries.9472742fc30fa1e420806a3c2bb0e7e11b4d11ef: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13697"/><div sID="gen26262" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13697"/><hi type="bold">4. And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female--</hi>or better, perhaps, "He that made them made them from the beginning a male and a female." <div eID="gen26262" type="x-p"/>
entries.ba15e25b0b81c7b8009bd064e15fe035b4de5856: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13698"/><div sID="gen26263" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13698"/><hi type="bold">5. And said, For this cause--</hi>to follow out this divine appointment.<div eID="gen26263" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26264" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?--</hi>Jesus here sends them back to the original constitution of man as one pair, a male and a female; to their marriage, as such, by divine appointment; and to the purpose of God, expressed by the sacred historian, that in all time one man and one woman should by marriage become one flesh--so to continue as long as both are in the flesh. This being God's constitution, let not man break it up by causeless divorces. <div eID="gen26264" type="x-p"/>
entries.161a3ccecb8143cb7d16bd86fdb2dc694ecc6c2f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13699"/><div sID="gen26265" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13699"/>7. They say unto him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? <div eID="gen26265" type="x-p"/>
entries.8b6527427f19c516daa26b070586507fa1bded75: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13700"/><div sID="gen26266" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13700"/><hi type="bold">8. He saith unto them, Moses--</hi>as a civil lawgiver.<div eID="gen26266" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26267" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">because of--</hi>or "having respect to."<div eID="gen26267" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26268" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the hardness of your hearts--</hi>looking to your low moral state, and your inability to endure the strictness of the original law.<div eID="gen26268" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26269" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">suffered you to put away your wives--</hi>tolerated a relaxation of the strictness of the marriage bond--not as approving of it, but to prevent still greater evils.<div eID="gen26269" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26270" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">But from the beginning it was not so--</hi>This is repeated, in order to impress upon His audience the temporary and purely civil character of this Mosaic relaxation. <div eID="gen26270" type="x-p"/>

And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except, &c.--</hi>See on <reference osisRef="Matt.5.32">Mt 5:32</reference>. <div eID="gen26271" type="x-p"/>
entries.af40e8e7d72fc1abcfa9881896dd25372f1d6f29: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13702"/><div sID="gen26272" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13702"/><hi type="bold">10. His disciples say unto him, If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry--</hi>that is, "In this view of marriage, surely it must prove a snare rather than a blessing, and had better be avoided altogether." <div eID="gen26272" type="x-p"/>
entries.49c19192cbb1cf8a11bda3109310c7de252e87a4: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13703"/><div sID="gen26273" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13703"/><hi type="bold">11. But he said unto them, All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given--</hi>that is, "That the unmarried state is better, is a saying not for everyone, and indeed only for such as it is divinely intended for." But who are these? they would naturally ask; and this our Lord proceeds to tell them in three particulars. <div eID="gen26273" type="x-p"/>
entries.a0dc88f882b97ca61a3bee6ad099c6aa92f8a756: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13704"/><div sID="gen26274" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13704"/><hi type="bold">12. For there are some eunuchs which were so born from their mother's womb--</hi>persons constitutionally either incapable of or indisposed to marriage.<div eID="gen26274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26275" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and there are some eunuchs which were made eunuchs of men--</hi>persons rendered incapable by others.<div eID="gen26275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26276" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and there be eunuchs which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake--</hi>persons who, to do God's work better, deliberately choose this state. Such was Paul (<reference osisRef="1Cor.7.7">1Co 7:7</reference>).<div eID="gen26276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26277" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">He that is able to receive it, let him receive it--</hi>"He who feels this to be his proper vocation, let him embrace it"; which, of course, is as much as to say--"he only." Thus, all are left free in this matter.<div eID="gen26277" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Matt.19.13-Matt.19.15">Mt 19:13-15</reference>. Little Children Brought to Christ.
